title: Semi-fractality and localization on a chiral Cayley tree
authors: Carlo Vanoni, Vladimir E. Kravtsov, Boris L. Altshuler
abstract: We study a quantum particle hopping on an infinite Cayley tree with nearest-neighbor hopping amplitudes drawn from a distribution singular as $|t|^{-a}$ near weak links and no on-site disorder. Because the graph is bipartite, the model has chiral symmetry, which strongly affects the statistics of eigenstates at the center of the spectrum. Using population dynamics to solve the cavity equations for the propagator, we analyze the distribution of the local density of states and show that it develops broad power-law tails. These tails imply an unusual form of wave-function statistics, which we call semi-fractality: the eigenstates occupy an extensive fraction of the system, but their higher moments behave as in a multifractal state. We find that the symmetry properties of the local-density-of-states distribution are not fixed only by the symmetry class, but vary continuously with the exponent controlling the power-law hopping distribution. As this exponent is changed, the system crosses from a semi-fractal regime to a localized one. At the transition, the wave functions realize an extreme intermediate form that we call semi-localized, simultaneously extended in their support but localized according to higher moments.
summary: The paper analyzes quantum particle hopping on a chiral Cayley tree with power-law disorder, revealing novel phases of eigenfunction statistics. It demonstrates that the system transitions between 'semi-fractal' and localized states as a function of the disorder exponent '$a$'. This transition is fundamentally linked to the preservation of chiral symmetry.
main_problem: The study investigates the nature of quantum wave function statistics—specifically semi-fractality and localization—for a particle hopping on an infinite Cayley tree.
main_result: The system exhibits a continuous transition between a 'semi-fractal' regime (characterized by power-law tails in LDoS) and a localized state, mediated by the chiral symmetry of the Hamiltonian.
method: The analysis employs population dynamics to solve cavity equations for the propagator, relating moments of the Local Density of States ($\langle ho^q angle$) to those of wave function amplitudes ($\langle |\psi|^{2q} angle$).
model_or_system: The model is a quantum particle hopping on an infinite Cayley tree with nearest-neighbor hopping amplitudes drawn from a power-law distribution $p(t) \propto |t|^{-a}$, possessing chiral symmetry due to the graph's bipartite nature.
key_observables: Local Density of States (LDoS) distribution, fractal dimensions ($D_q$), and the multifractal spectrum $f(\alpha)$.
important_parameters: The hopping exponent '$a$' acts as a tuning parameter controlling the transition between regimes; chiral symmetry is crucial.
main_assumptions: The analysis assumes the system maintains chiral symmetry (zero energy, link disorder only) and uses approximations relating LDoS moments to wave function moment averages.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the dependence of fractal dimensions ($D_q$) on the exponent $a$, showing distinct behaviors for semi-fractal ($ eta>1$) versus localized ($ eta<1$) regimes.
paper_structure: The paper establishes a relationship between LDoS moments and wave function moments, derives explicit formulas for $D_q$ in different parameter regimes ($ eta$), and discusses the physical interpretation of these fractal structures via eigenstate weight hierarchies.
why_interesting: This work provides a detailed theoretical framework connecting graph topology (Cayley tree), specific symmetries (chiral symmetry), and emergent wave function statistics (semi-fractality/localization) in disordered quantum systems, which is highly relevant to understanding transport in complex media.

FIG. 3. Top panel: Example of a semi-fractal Dq with β = 1.5. The solid line corresponds to Dq with the rare events with large wave function amplitudes (shown by the dashed line in the inset) taken into account, while the dashed line corresponds to Dq deduced from the typical average of the moments. In the inset, the corresponding spectrum of fractal dimensions is shown, which has a linear segment f(α) = β(α− 1)+1 with the slope β = 1.5 for α < 1 and the reciprocal linear segment with the slope γ −β −2 = −1.4 that corresponds to the Mirlin-Fyodorov symmetry with γ = 2.1. Bottom panel: Dq for β < 1, corresponding to the localized case. The inset shows the corresponding f(α).
